title: Emerging nonvolatile memory endurance-density tradeoff
bottleneck: Resistive RAM, MRAM, and FeRAM promise fast, dense, nonvolatile storage, but each trades endurance against density: filament-based ReRAM wears out with cycling, STT-MRAM struggles with write energy and retention at small cells, and ferroelectric devices face imprint and scaling limits. None has yet matched DRAM endurance with NAND-like density at competitive cost.
why_it_blocks: A universal memory would collapse the memory hierarchy, enabling instant-on systems and cheap in-memory computing; its absence forces complex tiered architectures and constant data shuffling. AI and edge systems pay the complexity tax in power, latency, and design effort.
current_state: Embedded MRAM is shipping in MCUs and some SoCs, and ReRAM appears in niche products. Standalone high-density, high-endurance emerging NVM at DRAM-class cost remains unproven.
